actions.label: Reproduce Find My Mouse game suppression behavior

reproduce.expected: Configured game suppression should have documented mode coverage without disabling ordinary desktop use or incorrectly claiming all borderless windows are games.
steps: On a current test system compare Find My Mouse activation in the same game exclusive-fullscreen, borderless and ordinary windowed modes with suppression enabled.
Record the Windows notification-state result and compare a borderless non-game application as a false-positive control.
Evaluate supported game-state APIs or a per-application exclusion path before changing the shared helper used by other modules.
prerequisites: Use a disposable test environment and test-owned documents/configuration; preserve existing user data.

known_information: A maintainer explicitly confirmed the old suppression only detected native fullscreen, and the reporter named several affected games.
Later affected users still report borderless cases; the latest maintainer reply explicitly says nobody is working on it.
Current FindMyMouse.StartSonar calls detect_game_mode, whose shared helper checks SHQueryUserNotificationState for QUNS_RUNNING_D3D_FULL_SCREEN. That is not a general borderless-game detector.
inferences: The proposed mechanism is provisional and is not an executed runtime result or evidence that the old report is fixed.
issue_context.summary: Investigate borderless-game suppression separately from exclusive fullscreen
issue_context.analysis: The existing fullscreen-notification heuristic does not establish whether an ordinary borderless foreground window is a game. Evaluate a supported game-state signal or explicit application exclusion while preserving desktop activation; do not infer gaming from GPU load or silently suppress every borderless application.
